item.title: Iran Says It Would Reopen Strait of Hormuz in 2 Days as Part of U.S. Deal
item.description: Iranian officials spoke of some progress in negotiating to reopen the strait even as they prepared for all-out war. A Qatari delegation arrived in Tehran on Monday to meet with the foreign minister to continue talks.

item.title: Netanyahu and Eisenkot Seek Shot to Be Israel’s Premier
item.description: Party leaders will make competing cases to the Israeli president for either Benjamin Netanyahu or Gadi Eisenkot to get the first chance to build a governing coalition.

item.title: King Charles Meets Both Joy and Criticism on Caribbean Tour
item.description: During the king’s visits to three former colonies, many people came out for celebratory parades and events. Others said the British state needed to atone for slavery’s toll.

item.title: Up in the Clouds With the Pope, It’s Still Commercial
item.description: Unlike American presidents, Pope Leo XIV has no private jet, so he travels on commercial airlines, like the rest of us. Well, almost.

item.title: Odyssey ‘Endless Cruise’ Ship Stranded in Cambodia May Be Headed for Auction Block
item.description: Efforts to pull together more funding for the ship, stuck in Cambodia, appear to have faltered, leaving its passengers unsure about what to do next.
